_readme: Valoris technology tree. Edit and run /valoris tech reload (op) to apply.
Technologies belong to a REALM: a kingdom, or a city in no kingdom. The king (or the ruler of
a free city) researches once the prerequisites ('requires') are known and the BEST levels among all
members of the realm meet 'skills' (blacksmith, farmer, miner, hunter). One research at a time per realm.
researchMinutes: real time the research takes (it keeps running while the server is off; saved immediately).
'starting': true = every city knows it from the start. x / y: column and row in the tree screen.
claimLimit: the city may claim this many chunks once it knows the technology (the highest known value counts).
features: what the GUI lists under 'Unlocks' (Armory Table items of the technology are shown automatically).
Unlock rules (matching items cannot be crafted until the city has that technology; '_' in ids is ignored):
item:<id>               one item, e.g. item:minecraft:iron_sword
mod:<namespace>         every item of a mod, e.g. mod:create
armor:<key>             Epic Knights armor type key ('key', 'key_helmet', 'key_chestplate', ...)
shield:<key>            Epic Knights shield type key without a material prefix (e.g. republicscutum)
shieldmaterial:<prefix> shields '<prefix>_<shield type>', e.g. shieldmaterial:steel
material:<prefix>       any tool/weapon/armor '<prefix>_...', e.g. material:steel
alwaysLocked: never craftable (a technology unlocking the item by name still wins; one unlocking its whole mod does not). disabledBlocks: cannot be placed/used.
cookingRestricted: results that vanilla furnaces/smokers/blast furnaces (and Create fans) may not produce;
iron and steel come only from the bloomery / steel furnace. '#tag' entries are item tags.
weaponBalance: damage = materials[material] + (types[type] - referenceBase) for items '<material>_<type>';
itemMaterials gives the material of weapons without a material prefix (e.g. magistuarmory:club).
version: when the built-in file has a higher version, this file is replaced (old copy kept as .bak).
Axes ('<material>_axe', type "axe") deal less than the weapons of their material.
